subtitle: Read it later, on your own server
description:
Shelf keeps the articles you mean to read. Paste a link, click the Save to Shelf button in your browser, share from your phone, or ask Claude to save something it found. Shelf fetches the page on your server and keeps a clean copy: the article's words and pictures, without the ads and pop-ups, so it's still there when the site changes.

The reader is set in Newsreader, a typeface made for reading on screens, in the size and width you like, on white or a paper tone, in light or dark. Shelf keeps your place and takes you back to it on any device. Select words to highlight them or add a note; your highlights gather in one place and find their spot again if the article is fetched afresh.

Ask for a three-point summary from your server's AI, or listen: your device reads the article aloud, a sentence at a time, and the page follows along. Search finds words inside the articles and your highlights, not only in titles.

Bring your links from Pocket, Instapaper or a bookmarks file. Connect Shelf to Claude and it can list, read and search your shelf, quote your highlights and save links for you.

It feels like an app: frosted bars that stay put, the article beside the list on a desk and sliding over it on a phone, swipes to archive and favourite, keys for everything on a desk, and articles that read offline.
whatsNew: Listening says so when a device has no voices, instead of stopping silently. On a phone, Summarise moves into the ⋯ menu so the reader’s bar has room, and the Archive label shows as you swipe a row.
